# cdpilot

> cdpilot is a zero-npm-dependency browser automation CLI for Chrome/Brave/Chromium, built directly on the raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) instead of Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium. It ships as a single Python core file plus a small Node.js launcher (~0.6MB npm package, no node_modules tree), exposes 70+ CLI commands, and includes a built-in MCP server (42 tools) so AI coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP client — can browse, click, fill forms, and read pages via structured accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots (structured text with @ref handles the agent can act on directly, no vision model needed). It also has LLM-free "smart" commands (click/fill by visible text, no CSS selectors, no LLM call needed), 10 built-in test assertions, and a progressive anti-bot layer (three-tier stealth, CAPTCHA + press-and-hold solvers, friction-ladder detection). MIT licensed, free and open source.

## Install

```bash
# no install needed
npx cdpilot launch      # start an isolated Chrome/Brave session with CDP enabled
npx cdpilot go https://example.com
npx cdpilot shot         # screenshot

# or install globally
npm i -g cdpilot
```

Requirements: Node.js 18+, Python 3.10+, and one of Brave/Chrome/Chromium. The Python
`websockets` package (cdpilot's only non-stdlib dependency) is auto-installed by the
setup wizard on first launch — there are 0 npm dependencies.

## MCP configuration

Claude Code (`.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add`) and Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json` or a
project `.cursor/mcp.json`) both read the same `mcpServers` schema:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cdpilot": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["cdpilot", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Key commands

- `cdpilot launch` — start a browser with CDP enabled, in an isolated profile
- `cdpilot setup` — auto-detect installed browsers, create the isolated profile
- `cdpilot go <url>` — navigate
- `cdpilot shot [file]` / `cdpilot pdf [file]` — screenshot / save page as PDF
- `cdpilot click <selector>` / `cdpilot smart-click <text>` — click by CSS selector, or by visible text with no LLM call
- `cdpilot fill <selector> <value>` / `cdpilot smart-fill <label> <value>` — set an input's value
- `cdpilot a11y-snapshot` — structured accessibility-tree snapshot with `@ref` navigation; measured 1.4-42x smaller than raw HTML across four sample pages (methodology and full numbers: [retraction notice](https://cdpilot.ndr.ist/blog/cdp-vs-playwright-benchmark))
- `cdpilot eval <js>` / `cdpilot eval-batch <json>` — run JavaScript, or N expressions in one CDP round trip
- `cdpilot test [--watch]` / `cdpilot trace open <run>` — run `*.cdpt.js` test files and open a time-travel trace viewer
- `cdpilot assert ...` — 10 built-in test assertions (url, title, count, value, attr, visible/hidden, screenshot-diff, ...)
- `cdpilot watch start <url>` — continuous screencast so an agent can observe motion, not just a still frame
- `cdpilot mode [regular|stealth|undetected]` — three-tier anti-fingerprint stealth switch
- `cdpilot friction` — read-only progressive anti-bot detection (rate-limit → CAPTCHA → login wall → hard block)
- `cdpilot cookies save|load --host <host>` — cache and replay per-host cookies (e.g. a passed Cloudflare/DataDome challenge)
- `cdpilot context create` + `CDPILOT_TARGET` — isolated parallel browser contexts in a single browser
- `cdpilot mcp` — start the built-in MCP server for AI agents
- `cdpilot --timeout <seconds> <command>` (or `CDPILOT_TIMEOUT`) — cap any command's wall-clock; exits 124 on expiry
- Page commands start the browser if it is not running (`CDPILOT_NO_AUTOLAUNCH=1` restores the old error)

## Honest limitations

- No iframe interaction yet (GitHub issue #1). Shadow DOM: the text-based smart commands (`smart-click`, `smart-fill`, `smart-select`) search inside open shadow roots; CSS-selector commands do not pierce them yet (issue #3)
- Deliberately does not attach to your existing, already-logged-in browser session — it
  launches an isolated profile by design, and reuses sessions via `cookies save/load` instead
- Heavy JS-challenge anti-bot vendors are still hard: per its own Stealth Bench V1,
  PerimeterX 2/18 (11%), GeeTest 0/4 (0%), Kasada 0/1 (0%), Akamai 1/6 (17%) — cdpilot
  is an avoidance engine, not a CAPTCHA solver, and counts a blocked task as a failure
